chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, he elevated it, saying:

Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: 'When a sheep is slaughtered and skinned, or part of it is skinned before it dies, its eating is not permissible.' He said to him: 'May I be your ransom, my grandfather says to you: A man struck a cow with an axe, it fell, then he slaughtered it, but did not send the answer with him. He called Sa'idah, the slave-girl of Umm Farwa, and said to her:

Muhammad came to me with a letter from you, and I disliked sending the answer with him. If the man who slaughtered the cow, when he slaughtered it, the blood came out evenly, then eat and feed; and if it came out sluggishly, do not approach it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering an animal that is skinned before it dies?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that premature skinning renders the meat impermissible, emphasizing the necessity of complete death before processing. He further clarifies the condition of *istiqlal al-dam* (even blood flow) by recounting a narrative where a cow was struck and then slaughtered, distinguishing between permissible consumption when blood flows steadily and impermissibility when the flow is sluggish, thereby linking the physical state of the animal to the validity of the slaughter.
